title: Police Fire Tear Gas on Jharkhand Student Marchers as Ex-JPSC Chief Arrested
excerpt: A two-week protest over alleged exam fraud erupts into violent clashes at the state assembly, forcing government concessions and political intervention.
body:
• Police used lathi charge, tear gas, and water cannons against students marching to the Jharkhand Legislative Assembly on August 10
  • Former JPSC chairperson L. Khinagte arrested by CID over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations
  • Jharkhand government agreed to cancel three examinations; all three JPSC members resigned
  • BJP enforced statewide bandh on August 11, with over 200 ABVP members detained during clashes with police

Student protests over alleged examination fraud in Jharkhand turned violent on August 10 when police fired tear gas and used water cannons and batons against thousands of demonstrators marching to the state Legislative Assembly in Ranchi. The same day, investigators arrested the former chairperson of the Jharkhand Public Service Commission, marking a significant escalation in the two-week crisis.

Assembly March Triggers Police Crackdown

The confrontation erupted when protesters attempted a "Vidhan Sabha Gherao" — a siege of the state assembly. Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, whose indefinite hunger strike began on August 2, joined the march in an ambulance before being hospitalized at Sadar Hospital in Ranchi due to deteriorating health.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2087225825863373020

Police said some protesters turned violent, broke through barricades, and threw stones. Multiple students were injured in the lathi charge, with one protester telling NDTV, "My head is bleeding." Jharkhand Police reported 14 of their personnel were also injured during the clashes.

"The government will have to bow down because this is a fight for the students of the entire Jharkhand. This movement represents the voice of millions of young people who pursue their dreams through education and hard work."

— Devendra Nath Mahto, Student Leader, JLKM

How the Crisis Unfolded

The movement began on July 29 when candidates started a sit-in at Ranchi's Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium after a carbon copy of an OMR answer sheet went viral. The document allegedly showed that a candidate had qualified for the next stage of the JPSC civil services examination despite answering only 48 of 100 questions in the first paper.

The Jharkhand CID arrested the candidate, Suman Saurav, along with 10 others believed to be connected to the alleged paper leak. But the arrests failed to quell public anger. Students argue the incident is part of a long-standing pattern of paper leaks, delayed results, and recruitment irregularities that have plagued Jharkhand since its formation in 2000.

Protesters are demanding a CBI inquiry into irregularities involving both the JPSC and the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission, which oversees major recruitment examinations including Combined Graduate Level and Excise Constable exams.

Government Concessions and Arrests

Under mounting pressure, the Jharkhand government agreed on August 10 to cancel three examinations, according to The Indian Express. All three members of the JPSC resigned the same day. The CID arrested former JPSC chairperson and former Jharkhand Chief Secretary L. Khinagte over alleged irregularities in the recruitment process.

An 11-member student delegation has been formed to negotiate directly with the state government. During the monsoon session of the Jharkhand Assembly, which opened on August 6, opposition parties raised the exam controversy while 19 people were detained during demonstrations outside.

Political Fallout Widens

The BJP enforced a statewide bandh on August 11 to protest what it called "police atrocities" against students. More than 200 ABVP members were detained during their attempted march to the Legislative Assembly, with clashes erupting after some workers tried to stop a police van carrying detained members, according to The Indian Express.

Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi have expressed concern over the irregularities. The movement has also drawn support from the Cockroach Janta Party, which led nationwide protests over the NEET paper leak earlier this year. Education activist Sonam Wangchuk urged Mahto to drink water as his hunger strike extended past its fourth day.

"Transparency must be brought into the system; the old ways won't work in Jharkhand anymore because the students here have become aware."

— Archana Kumari, Student Protester

What's Next

Despite government concessions, the student movement shows no sign of ending. Protesters say the exam cancellations and JPSC resignations address symptoms rather than the systemic corruption they allege pervades Jharkhand's recruitment process. Their core demand — a CBI-led investigation — remains unmet.

The protests echo a broader pattern of youth frustration with competitive examination systems that govern access to government employment in India — a pipeline that millions of families view as a path to economic stability. The crisis adds to a year of student-led movements across the country, from the NEET paper leak protests in Delhi to state-level agitations demanding accountability in public recruitment.
nri_angle: The examination fraud crisis reflects systemic issues in India's public sector recruitment that contribute to skilled professionals seeking opportunities abroad.
author: Diaspora Desk
